text:
maya: Heads up — SLO alert for proxy-eu-west: mTLS handshake success rate down to ~88% over the last 15m. Seems correlated with yesterday's RBAC change to the audit-sampling role. Anyone touching KMS keywrap/policy? :eyes:

devops-bot: ALERT: [SLO] mtls_handshake_rate_slo_eu triggered for service=proxy-eu-west (15m avg=88.3%). Runbook: eng-security -> triage.

troy: Oncall I can pick this up. Maya, can you paste the first failing logs or the error pattern?

maya: Copying a few lines from the proxy-ingress logs. Looks like KMS decrypt/unwrap denies around the same time: 

```
2026-03-21T10:02:13Z proxy-eu-west auth=mtls handshake_ok=false err="kms.DecryptAccessDenied" key=projects/redwood/locations/eu/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/keystore-ephemeral
2026-03-21T10:02:14Z proxy-eu-west auth=mtls handshake_ok=false err="certstore.unable_to_unwrap" subject=service-a.redwood.internal
```

jess: I pushed an RBAC tweak to reduce audit sampling noise yesterday at 03:10 UTC — I added binding `roles/audit.sampler` to `group:infra-audit` and removed a permissive grant on `proxy-keystore` service account. Patch id: patch/infra-2026-03-20-03. I'm re-checking now.

nikhil: That removal could explain it. If the proxy-keystore SA lost `cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` on the ephemeral key we get unwrap denies -> handshake failures. Quick check: I ran a dry-run against KMS IAM earlier: result shows `proxy-keystore@...` not bound to the key.

troy: If that's the case rollback is simplest. Two options: grant decrypt back to proxy-keystore or add an exceptions binding for the ephemeral keystore. Which is preferred?

jess: We intentionally locked down wide grants, but missed adding the least-priv role to the new group. I'll patch the key policy to add the exact SA. Will post the command in a sec.

nikhil: Also note audit sampling was lowered from 100% -> 10% in the same change, so we lost full handshake telemetry during the window. That makes debugging harder and could have compliance impact. Need to capture how many handshake events we lost.

kelsey: From compliance POV: if sampling dropped >1% of total handshakes for a regulated customer, we need to escalate. Can you quantify lost logs and retention gap?

maya: Ballpark numbers from metrics: proxy-eu-west ~12k handshakes in 15m, sampling 100%->10% -> ~10.8k events not persisted. Will refine.

devops-bot: metrics query: `sum(rate(mtls_handshakes_total{region="eu-west"}[15m])) = 800/s -> ~72000 / 15m` (example) — adjust accordingly.

jess: Command I'm about to run to grant decrypt back (will do with canary):
```
# grant decrypt to proxy-keystore SA on the key
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood/locations/eu/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/keystore-ephemeral
  --member="serviceAccount:proxy-keystore@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"
```

jess: Canarying on a single proxy node first. ping @troy when done.

troy: Ack. I'll watch the SLO and trace logs. If decrypts clear up, we'll roll to full fleet. Also prepare to revert sampling to 100% once we have stable handshakes for full telemetry.

nikhil: If we want a safer option without KMS changes, immediate fallback is to swap the proxy keystore to the previous static cert bundle (fallback-keystore) until we fix IAM. Command: `kubectl set env deploy/proxy KEYSOURCE=fallback-keystore --namespace=proxy-eu-west` — short-lived mitigation.

maya: Good call. Which approach is lower blast radius? jess to revert IAM is small scoped but touches KMS policy; swap to fallback-keystore affects rolling restarts. Your call.

jess: I'll do the KMS IAM add first as it's the smallest change. Will run canary and post results in 2m.

devops-bot: NOTE: audit-sampling-change event recorded: user=jess id=patch/infra-2026-03-20-03 sampling_rate=10% -> 100% previous=100% time=2026-03-20T03:10:00Z

(2m pass)
jess: Can confirm canary node now shows unwrap OK. Sample logs: `handshake_ok=true subject=service-a.redwood.internal` and no kms.DecryptAccessDenied.

troy: Observability: mTLS success rate jumped back to 97% in canary cluster. Rolling to rest of fleet now. Watch for any regressions.

kelsey: Please add an entry in compliance incident log with numbers and timeline (sampling window, lost event estimate, customers impacted). We may need to notify a few regs depending on threshold.

maya: Will open an incident ticket: INC-2026-031 — I'll include timeline, patch id, estimated lost events (10.8k in the 15m window), and corrective actions (IAM patch + restore sampling to 100% after validation).

nikhil: Postmortem checklist: root cause=RBAC change removed decrypt binding; contributing=sampling reduction obscured detection; fixes=IAM policy corrected, sampling restored, add automated pre-deploy check to validate key bindings for proxy-keystore.

jess: I'll file PR for a preflight script that runs `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` and verifies required members before merging RBAC changes.

troy: Also add an automated SLO alert that correlates KMS unwrap_denies with handshake drops so future incidents auto-pin to KMS IAM.

maya: Thanks all. Keeping the incident open until telemetry stabilizes and compliance log is updated. :white_check_mark: 

kelsey: I'll review the compliance note once you post it. Good triage speed everyone. :thumbsup:

(incident remains open, assigned to troy/jess/nikhil for follow-ups)
